title: Prompt-enhancement settings - the DeepInfra key, the Ollama models, and which LLM enhances
description:
Fabio, 2026-09-12, from MPI-677's step-1c user-ux pass. Enhancement has no settings surface at all, and three separate gaps land on the same one. (1) THE DEEPINFRA KEY HAS NOWHERE TO GO. `routes/llm.js` already tells the user to "add a DeepInfra key in settings" and no such field exists - the key only ever reached the app through the environment on a dev boot. (2) NOTHING HANDLES A MISSING OLLAMA MODEL, AND NOTHING STARTS OR INSTALLS OLLAMA. Grepped 2026-09-12: no `api/pull` anywhere in the repo, no presence check, no toast, no lifecycle - `ensureOllama` appears nowhere, and the only three files mentioning Ollama are routes/llm.js, services/llmEngines.mjs and js/services/llmService.js. A user with Ollama running but without the model gets `Ollama chat failed: 404 Not Found` raw. This is CONSOLIDATION DEBT: Cubric Prompt shipped the whole ladder as its MPI-8 (probe the server, spawn `ollama serve` detached, treat ENOENT as the not-installed signal, one-time remembered consent, then winget, download page as the fallback, never bundle Ollama, never stop it on quit) plus MPI-17 (the spawn must inherit the desktop app's configured model directory, recovered from the Ollama app's own server.log - never set OLLAMA_MODELS as a persistent var, it shadows what the user later picks; measured on Fabio's machine as 0 models reported against 9 models / 63.2 GB on disk). Step 1a ported the engine and the route and NONE of the lifecycle, and nothing recorded that it had not. (3) WHICH LLM ENHANCES IS NOT THE ONE THE RECIPES WERE MEASURED ON, AND THE USER CANNOT CHANGE IT. `chooseEngineModelId()` (js/services/llmService.js:166) returns UNCENSORED_MODEL_ID only when the TARGET model card's id ends in `-nsfw`; every other local enhance falls through to DEFAULT_MODEL_ID = `gemma-4-e4b` -> `gemma4:e4b`, and every cloud enhance to `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`. But MODEL_REGISTRY's own description of `gemma-4-abliterated-12b` says it is "the ENHANCER of record: every v1 recipe is Stage 1 green on this model. Word-budget adherence is a capability threshold between 8B and 12B, so recipes hold their length here and drift on smaller models" - and llmEngines.mjs's own header says these models ARE the instrument and changing one silently invalidates every green in docs/recipes/research/. So the shipped SFW path runs an enhancer on the wrong side of the stated threshold, no recipe was ever green on it, and this was never recorded as a decision. Backend has a preference (`cubric.llm.backend` in localStorage) with no UI; the enhancer MODEL has neither. SCOPE: a settings section that takes the DeepInfra key (main-side, never readable back - Cubric Prompt's safeStorage contract is the precedent), installs/pulls the Ollama model with progress and a presence check, exposes the backend preference that already exists, lets the user pick the enhancer model from MODEL_REGISTRY, and carries a short plain-English explanation of what enhancement does. OPEN FOR FABIO: whether the DEFAULT enhancer should move to the abliterated 12B (what the recipes were measured on) or stay on E4B (what most users can actually run) - that is a product call about the floor, not a bug, and if it moves it should be recorded as a decision rather than drifting. Parent: MPI-677 (the consolidation umbrella); the gaps were found during its step 1c.

--- 2026-09-12, MEASURED + FABIO'S DIRECTION (supersedes gap 3's framing) ---

GAP 3 IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS NOT "SWITCH THE DEFAULT". The dog experiment ran `a man walking his dog` through the `illustrious` t2v recipe, ten runs on each of three enhancers (MPI-677 validation.md). The shipped cloud model `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` kept the user's subject 10/10; the shipped local `gemma4:e4b` kept it 10/10; the ENHANCER OF RECORD `huihui_ai/gemma-4-abliterated:12b` kept it 4/10. The tell is sharper than the counts: the 12B keeps `holding leash` 9/10 while dropping the animal, i.e. it writes a man holding a leash attached to nothing. Promoting the 12B to default would INTRODUCE the defect it was being considered to fix. It does not settle the instrument question for every recipe (one recipe, one input) but it inverts the burden of proof.

FABIO'S CALL, 2026-09-12: THE USER PICKS THE ENHANCER, WITH GUIDANCE. Not an automatic route. "Gemma 4B should be fine, but the user should also have the possibility of choosing an uncensored model" - with feedback in the UI about which target models are uncensored and which LLMs suit which targets. So this card owns a PICKER plus explanatory copy, not a new hardcoded default.

AND THE ROUTING HEURISTIC IS WRONG IN THE FIELD. `isUncensoredModel()` derives "uncensored" from the `-nsfw` id suffix, and its own ponytail comment states the ceiling: "if that turns out to matter in the field, the fix is an explicit `uncensored: true` on those model defs, not a cleverer suffix rule". IT HAS NOW TURNED OUT TO MATTER. Fabio, 2026-09-12, listing what is actually uncensored in Vision: EVERY SDXL model - sdxl-realistic, ill-anime, ill-anime-beauty, pony-mix - plus sdxl-nsfw; BOTH Chroma models, which exist specifically for NSFW; and WAN 2.2, fine-tuned for it. LTX with a LoRA, and MiniMax likewise. His summary: "any model can do that using a LoRA that the user can just download from somewhere."

Only two of those carry `-nsfw`. So today every one of the others routes to `gemma4:e4b` or, with a key, to DEEPINFRA - a hosted provider being handed prompts for models built for uncensored output. That is the opposite of the rule `chooseBackend()` states in its own comment ("DeepInfra carries no abliterated model, so an uncensored card must never fall through to it").

Two consequences, and they pull in the same direction: a suffix cannot classify this (a LoRA makes any model uncensored, so the property is not a fact about the card at all), and an automatic route cannot either. A user-chosen enhancer with honest labelling is the design that survives both.

--- 2026-09-12, FABIO HARDENS IT: DELETE THE CLASSIFICATION, DO NOT REPLACE IT ---

"No more model tags or 'is uncensored', because every model can be uncensored. We need to clean up that code. And this way the user is the one who decides what model to use."

So an `uncensored: true` field on the model defs - which `isUncensoredModel()`'s own comment proposed as the fix - is REJECTED before it is built. The property was never a fact about the target card: a LoRA the user downloads makes any model uncensored, so a suffix and a boolean field are the same mistake at different resolutions.

THE REASON IS ABOUT THE USER, NOT THE MODEL. Fabio: a user who wants no violence and nothing explicit would never pick an uncensored LLM; the uncensored user is the inverse and needs one. The app cannot know which it is talking to, and the target model does not say. So the disposition belongs to the person, and the only honest place for it is a choice they make.

THE DELETION SURFACE IS FOUR PRODUCTION LINES IN ONE FILE (measured 2026-09-12):
  js/services/llmService.js:49   `export const UNCENSORED_MODEL_ID = 'gemma-4-abliterated-12b'`
  js/services/llmService.js:139  `export function isUncensoredModel(model)`
  js/services/llmService.js:160  `if (isUncensoredModel(model)) return canEnhanceInGraph(model) ? 'comfy' : 'ollama';`  (in chooseBackend)
  js/services/llmService.js:168  `return isUncensoredModel(model) ? UNCENSORED_MODEL_ID : undefined;`  (in chooseEngineModelId)
plus four assertions in tests/llm-service.test.cjs (:79, :87-90). Nothing else reads either symbol. The `-nsfw` ids elsewhere in the repo are model CARD NAMES (sdxl-nsfw, krea2-nsfw, klein-lora-nsfw) and product data - they stay; what goes is the inference drawn FROM the name.

ONE CONSEQUENCE TO DECIDE DELIBERATELY, NOT DISCOVER: line 160 is the ONLY thing that routes anything to the `comfy` backend. Delete it and the in-graph ComfyUI encoder becomes reachable only by an explicit user pin (`backendPreference()` already accepts 'comfy'). Under "the user decides" that is arguably the right answer, but it must be chosen rather than fall out of a deletion - the in-graph path exists because it reuses an encoder the generation already loaded instead of standing a second runtime beside it.

AND THE PICKER MUST COVER THE BACKEND, NOT ONLY THE MODEL. Deleting the rule also deletes the guarantee `chooseBackend()` states in its own comment - that an uncensored card never falls through to DeepInfra, which carries no abliterated model. Once the user is choosing, that guarantee becomes information they need rather than a rule the code enforces: a hosted provider will refuse or sanitise what a local abliterated build will shape. Say so where they choose.

MEASURED CAVEAT FOR THE COPY: uncensored is not a synonym for better. The abliterated 12B is the ENHANCER OF RECORD and it dropped the user's own subject 6 runs in 10 where both shipped models dropped none (MPI-677 validation.md, the dog experiment). Whatever the picker recommends, it must not imply the uncensored build is the stronger instrument.
